title.narrative: Output 1.2. Increased institutional capacity of workers’ organizations

description.narrative:
1. In May 2022, workers' organizations in the Philippines submitted a Joint Union Paper on “Labor’s Review of the SDG Goals and Targets for the 2022 Philippine Voluntary National Review (VNR)” to the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA). The Joint Union Paper summarizes the assessment and recommendations made by trade unions and other worker organizations on the state of the Philippines’ targets and achievements of SDGs 4 (Quality Education), 5 (Gender Equality), 14 (Life on Water), 15 (Life on Land), and 17 (Partnership for the Goals). The Joint Union Paper served as key inputs in the design of the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UN SDCF) for 2023 to 2028. 2. In December 2022, workers’ organizations developed and launched and the 15-Point Labour Agenda, with 5 key thematic areas covering freedom of association, security of tenure, living wages, decent job creation, social protection for all. The 15-Point Labour Agenda serves as the labour sector’s common blueprint in addressing issues that affect workers covering a period of 5 years, including joint union proposals on proposed bills addressing CEACR comments on C87 and COVID-19 responses, and beyond. Workers have used the Labour Agenda for labour-related policy inputs including in the Labor and Employment Plan (LEP) and UN SDCF for 2023 to 2028. 1.The ILO supported workers' organizations in the drafting of the paper and conduct of meetings to consolidate the positions of the various workers' organizations. Ten labor organizations—one national chapter of a global union federation, eight national trade unions (federations and confederations) in the private and public sector, and one national organization of workers in the informal sector participated in the collaborative and consultative process in coming up with a joint position paper.
2. The ILO provided support to workers' organizations through convening meetings, stakeholder discussions and regional/island-wide consultations to develop the Labour Agenda, prepare for workers’ position during the HLTM, and the promotion of the HLTM Recommendations and the Labour Agenda in the regions.

Output 1.2. Increased institutional capacity of workers’ organizations

description.narrative: Workers’ organizations in the Philippines submitted proposals for the design of new mechanisms that protect the rights and life of trade union activists during the High-level Tripartite Mission (HLTM) in Jan 2023. The workers' proposal for enhanced services to all workers included the design of protective systems of a Presidentially mandated body to ensure that provisions of C87 are better protected, a truth commission mechanism being formed to compensate to victims and prosecution on violations, and enhancing the existing monitoring bodies on FOA violations. The HLTM accepted the submitted proposals as being viable steps on amicably moving towards ensuring C87 is better protected. As of Apr 2023, Government formed the Presidential body, through Executive Order (EO)23, and has pursued further development and amendments to ensure commitment to the agreements to the ILO and also to the social partners through the development of a tripartite FOA roadmap to ensure effective follow through. In May 2023, workers’ organizations replicated the unity forged at the national level by launching a regional alliance in Central Visayas. This has resulted to unified proposed recommendations on the EO 23 and FOA Roadmap in support to HLTM recommendations. Workers’ organizations have embraced the advent of digitalization as an innovative way to continue organizing, especially as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic’s impact on the exercise of FOA and the right to organize. In 2023, trade unions rolled-out to its members the expanded FOA monitoring tool, which now includes the use of digital tools to monitor and report cases and to promote labour rights education. In July 2023, the Associated Labor Unions-Trade Union Congress of the Philippines established partnership with workers associations in the highly informal small-scale miners associations to push for amendments to the Small Scale Mining Act, supporting formalisation and improved working conditions in the industry. With support from the European Union and with contribution from RBSA, the ILO provided technical support through conduct of meetings, research, technical reviews of documentation, coordination with ILO departments and officials on the design of the proposals submitted by the workers. Furthermore, the ILO supported the development of an FOA and labour rights digital monitoring tool, which can be used by workers and trade unions in reporting, documenting cases and incidents of alleged FOA and labour rights violations, for later collective workers/unions’ action. The ILO also supported the updating and digitalization of the Workers’ FOA Case Build-Up Module and E-Learning Platform, which is meant to promote the capacity-building of workers and union organizers and enhance labour rights education through both synchronous and asynchronous modes of learning. With the support of the United States Department of Labor, the ILO supported the organizing of small-scale mining associations in selected communities and supported the formation of the National Coalition of Small-Scale Miners’ Association of the Philippines, Inc (NCSSMPI) from 2016 to 2019. In 2021, the ILO organized several inter-union activities that enabled building of linkages between different workers’ organisations, and led to ALU TUCP collaborating with small-scale mining associations, including consultations on proposed amendments on the existing law for small-scale mines and advocating for the small-scale mining associations with the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB).
